newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up 4.87 pct after all-day rally.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up 4.87 pct after all-day rally.

text.p: Thai stocks ended sharply up 4.87 percent in active trade on Monday as investors bought stocks across the board after welcome news that a general election would be held on November 17, brokers said.

The SET index hit its intraday peak at 1,101.74-point, or up 53.79, at 0754 GMT, surpassing a strong resistance level at 1,100-point. But it retreated later and closed at 1,099.01, up 51.06 points, on active 13.3 billion baht trade. The SET-50 index rose 4.54 points to 84.56.
"The buying was mainly bargain hunting by speculators and was in response to the welcome election news," said a broker.
The index closing level today was the highest hit by market since August 30 when it finished at 1,102.32.
Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa dissolved parliament on Friday and set the new polls date then.

"The rise in the index won't last long. It will rise for a maximum of one week because there are really no strong fundamentals to back it up," said Witawus Charuchandr of Ekachart Finance and Securities. Locals were most active.
Brokers said investors, especially foreigners, still remained concerned about the slowing Thai economy, especially sagging exports. They were also awaiting a new government.

The central bank on Thursday released key economic indicators showing sustained weak exports which rose a marginal 2.9 percent year-on-year during January-July against hefty 26.5 percent growth seen in the same period a year ago.
The finance sector topped the board, gaining 8.11 percent, followed by the communication sector which rose 8.02 percent.
Finance One rose eight baht to 108. Bangkok Bank advanced eight to 228 and Banpu rose 16 to 550.
Support is seen at 1,080-point and resistance at 1,120 on Tuesday, brokers said. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
